title: Verb 'to be' (am/is/are)
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu yɛ adwuma foforo biara: 'wɔ' ne 'yɛ'. Wɔ English mu na yɛ 'to be' foforo. Nkyɛn kyɛn no yɛ sɛ wɔ Twi mu na yɛde 'wɔ/yɛ' ma akwa ne ahwɛyiye, sɛnea English biara. Nnini pii no yɛ sɛ wɔ English mu mmom ahwɛyiye no nni hɔ: ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'I am', 'you are', 'he is', etc. ma.
rule: Verb 'to be' wɔ present mu no wɔ atwɔnva: 'am' (ma 'I'), 'is' (ma 'he, she, it') ne 'are' (ma 'you, we, they'). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wobu asɛm biara a, yɛde kyerɛw asɛm no: 'Are you...?', 'Is he...?'. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wone asɛm biara a, yɛde 'not' ma: 'I am not', 'he is not' (anaa 'he isn't'), 'they are not' (anaa 'they aren't').

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu yɛde 'Mewɔ anim' without auxiliary verb, nanso wɔ English mu verb 'to be' no yɛ de paa. Nnya 'am/is/are' no.

examples.note: Yɛde 'am' ma 'I' mmom.
Yɛde 'is' ma third person singular.
Short form 'aren't' yɛ common wɔ conversation mu.
Yɛde subject ne verb no ma asɛm biara.

title: Personal Pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, mmebusɛm a wɔde kɔda ni home ha wɔ hɔ: me, wo, ɔno, ɔbaa, yɛ, wɔn. Nnipa pii a wɔtɔ mmebusɛm no mu no, wɔde no kɔda ni home sɛ wɔde no kɔda ni kyɛn saa Araba mu no, na ɛno a ɛyɛ den sɛn na wɔde 'he' ne 'she' kɔda ni home — wɔ Araba mu no, ɛnte saa efie ne nnwuma a ɛde kɔda ni home no sɛ wɔ Twi mu no.
rule: Mmebusɛm a wɔde kɔda ni home wɔ Araba mu no ne: I (me), you (wo/wɔn), he (ɔno), she (ɔbaa), it (ɛno), we (yɛ), they (wɔn). 'It' de kɔda ni efie, anantwi ne nnwuma. 'You' de kɔda ni ni ne nnipa pii. Wɔ Araba mu no, ɛnyɛ nea ɛho hwee sɛ wode mmebusɛm kɔda ni home.

concept_examples.translation: Yɛne yɛ nnipa a wɔde akɔso.

common_error.correct: He is a teacher. / She is a teacher.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu no, yɛbɛka 'Ɔno ne obi a ɔde akɔso' na yɛntɔ mmebusɛm no, nanso wɔ Araba mu no, mmebusɛm no yɛ da. Ɛsɛ sɛ woka 'He is...' anaa 'She is...'.

levels.label: Singular pronouns
levels.translation: Mmebusɛm a wɔde kɔda ni ni

examples.note: Ni a ɛyɛ ni.

levels.label: Third person singular
levels.translation: Ni a ɛyɛ ni a ɛyɛ ɔno

examples.note: Ma obi a ɔdwen ne mma ne mma.

levels.label: Plural pronouns
levels.translation: Mmebusɛm a wɔde kɔda ni nnipa pii

examples.translation: Wɔn ne me mama ne me papa.
examples.note: Ma nnipa pii anaa efie pii.
'It' de kɔda ni efie, anantwi ne nnwuma.

title: Nnwom (a/an, the)
bridge: Wɔ Twi so na yɛn nso yɛ nnwom: 'obaa/oba' (mframa nnwom) ne 'wɔ' (nnwom a ɛho nhwɛso). Nkyɛnkyɛn a ɛso ntɛm ne sɛ wɔ Twi mmom yɛnntɔn 'the' ma yɛde kasa kyerɛɛ nnyinasosɛm (yɛbɛka 'Life is beautiful', na ɛnyɛ 'The life is beautiful'). Sɛ yɛkaa profesioni a, yɛde 'a' anaa 'an' ma: 'I am a teacher' (wɔ Twi yɛbɛka 'Me wɔ kɔkɔɔ' mframa nnwom).
rule: Yɛde 'a' ma nnwom a ɛtɔ so kɔnsonant (a book, a car). Yɛde 'an' ma nnwom a ɛtɔ so vowel (an apple, an hour — 'h' nni hɔ). Yɛde 'the' ma yɛde kyerɛ sɛm bi a ɛyɛ anaa ɛde maa yɛakyi. Yɛmmɔ 'the' ma yɛde kyerɛ nnyinasosɛm (Love is important, na ɛnyɛ 'The love').

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi yɛbɛka 'Me wɔ kɔkɔɔ' mframa nnwom. Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛkaa profesioni a, yɛde 'a' anaa 'an' ma.

examples.note: Yɛde 'a' ma nnwom a ɛtɔ so kɔnsonant.
Yɛde 'an' ma nnwom a ɛtɔ so vowel.
'The' de ma yɛde kyerɛ sɛm bi a ɛyɛ anaa ɛde maa yɛakyi.
Sɛ yɛkaa nnyinasosɛm a, yɛmmɔ 'the'.

title: Mmusu̩ regular na mmusu̩ aben̩fo̩ basic
bridge: W̩ ha w̩-Koranii, yɛbɔ mmusu̩ wɔde yɛ’s’ anaa ’es’ too so (casa → casas, reloj → relojes). Wɔ Twitwim ma wɔyɛe yie: mmerɛwo wɔde ’s’ too (book → books), nanso wɔhyɛ mmerɛma no ho nhyehyɛe: sɛ mmerɛma no kyerɛw wɔ ’s’, ’sh’, ’ch’, ’x’, ’z’ a, wɔde ’es’ too (bus → buses, watch → watches). Wɔhyɛ mmerɛma mmusu̩ aben̩fo̩ nso (child → children, foot → feet) wɔde yɛ mmusu̩ a wɔnnyɛ nhyehyɛe no ho. Ɛwom wɔn a wɔsɛe wɔn.
rule: Nhyehyɛe ma mmusu̩ regular: 1) De ’s’ too (cat → cats). 2) De ’es’ too sɛ mmerɛma no kyerɛw wɔ ’s’, ’sh’, ’ch’, ’x’, ’z’ (box → boxes, dish → dishes). 3) Sɛ ɛkyerɛw wɔ ’y’ na ɛwɔ awerɛho a, hwɛ ’y’ maa ’ies’ (city → cities). 4) Sɛ ɛkyerɛw wɔ ’f’ anaa ’fe’ a, mmerɛma pii de ’ves’ (wolf → wolves, knife → knives). Mmusu̩ aben̩fo̩ no yɛ mmerɛma a wɔnnyɛ nhyehyɛe: child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, man → men, woman → women, mouse → mice, sheep → sheep (sɛe), fish → fish (sɛe ma ɔno ara).

common_error.explanation: Wɔ w̩-Koranii, mmusu̩ nyinaa yɛ regular (niño → niños), nanso wɔ Twitwim, 'child' yɛ aben̩fo̩ na ɛmmusu̩ yɛ 'children'. Ɛyɛ akannsɔfo̩ a wɔde w̩-Koranii kasa no sɛnnoma a wɔde ’s’ too no ho adwuma.

examples.note: Mmusu̩ regular wɔ’s’ too.
Mmerɛma a wɔkyerɛw wɔ ’x’ de ’es’ too.
Siane a (a → e).
Mmusu̩ no yɛ sɛ mmerɛma no ara.

title: Presente simple (I eat, you eat, he eats)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyɛ present tense ma awoɔ kronkron: 'Mɛnka pizza da biara'. Wɔ English, sɛ yɛayɛ paa, nanso wɔ 3rd person (he, she, it) yɛma -s ase kan verb no (he eats, she works). Yɛn nso yɛbɛhyia auxiliary 'do/does' maa yɛbisa ne yɛntumi, sɛnea yɛde '...?' kyerɛkyerɛ wɔ Twi, nanso wɔ English no yɛn ho adanse.
rule: Present simple no yɛde verb base maa wɔn nyinaa nkyɛn, nkyɛnkyɛ 3rd person singular (he, she, it) no, yɛde -s maa no (anaa -es sɛ verb no kuraa -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z). Maa yɛbisa ne yɛntumi, yɛde 'do' (maa I, you, we, they) anaa 'does' (maa he, she, it) + verb base (bi -s). Mfatie: 'I eat', 'He eats', 'Do you eat?', 'She doesn't eat'.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, 3rd person singular no nni ho nhyehyɛe wɔ present tense (ɔno nka), nanso wɔ English no yɛma -s ase da biara (he eats). Yei ne mmara pii a wɔde kɔ so wɔ Twi kasafoɔ.

examples.note: Verb wɔ base form.

examples.original: She reads a book every day.
examples.translation: Ɔbaa no kenkan book da biara.
examples.note: Yɛama -s ase verb no.
'Does' + subject + verb base (bi -s).
Yɛde 'don't' + verb base.

title: Nsɛmfuadaneho asɛm (always, sometimes, never)
bridge: Hɔn akan mu, nsɛmfuadaneho asɛm a wɔn ka ne 'siempre', 'a veces' ne 'nunca' bɛka ho asɛm a, wɔde wɔn hyɛn verb no anim: 'Yo siempre como pizza' anaa wɔde wɔn hyɛn verb no a ɛyɛ akyire abiɛsa. Hɔn a wɔde wɔn asɛm hyɛn verb 'to be' akyire no (I am always tired). Nkyɛnkyɛn a ɛyɛ ne sɛ, hɔn akan mu, ɛbɛyɛ abodwene sɛ wode nsɛmfuadaneho asɛm no hyɛn verb a ɛyɛ anim (I always eat pizza), na ɛbɛyɛ abodwene sɛ wode no hyɛn verb 'to be' akyire (I am always tired). Nkyɛn a ɛyɛ ne sɛ, hɔn akan mu, ɛbɛyɛ abodwene sɛ wode nsɛmfuadaneho asɛm no hyɛn verb a ɛyɛ anim, na ɛnyɛ abodwene sɛ wode no hyɛn verb a ɛyɛ akyire.
rule: Nsɛmfuadaneho asɛm a wɔn ka ne: always (siempre), usually (normalmente), often (a menudo), sometimes (a veces), rarely (raramente), never (nunca). Wɔde wɔn hyɛn verb a ɛyɛ anim (I always go to school), na wɔde wɔn hyɛn verb 'to be' akyire (I am always happy). Sɛ wubisa a, de no hyɛn subject no akyire (Do you always eat breakfast?)

concept_examples.text: I always drink coffee in the morning.
concept_examples.translation: Me siempre bebɛ café por la mañana.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɔːlweɪz drɪŋk ˈkɒfi ɪn ðə ˈmɔːnɪŋ/

concept_examples.translation: Ɔbaa no nunca lɛgyea afe a ɛyɛ akyire.

concept_examples.text: They sometimes go to the cinema.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔyɛ mmarima no a veces bɛka cine.
Wɔbisa sɛ, wɔ a menudo di kan?

common_error.explanation: Hɔn akan mu, yɛka sɛ 'Me siempre comɛ pizza' anaa 'Me comɛ pizza siempre'. Hɔn a wɔde wɔn asɛm hyɛn verb 'to be' akyire no, nsɛmfuadaneho asɛm no bɛka verb a ɛyɛ anim (always eat). Sɛ wode no hyɛn verb a ɛyɛ akyire a, ɛbɛto abodwene sɛ wɔde hɔn akan no asɛm no kyerɛw wo kwan.

examples.original: I always get up at 7 am.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɔːlweɪz ɡet ʌp æt ˈsevən æm/
examples.translation: Me siempre mɛtrɛw a ɛyɛ 7 a ɛyɛ aman.
examples.note: Frecuencia máxima.

examples.translation: Ɔbɔfo no a veces rebɛ television.
examples.note: Frecuencia media.

examples.translation: Yɛn nunca yɛ di fast food.
examples.note: Frecuencia nula (negativo).
El adverbio va DESPUÉS del verbo 'to be'.

title: Have got / Has got
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka biribi a ɔte ase yɛn ho a, yɛnka ‘tener’. ‘Yo tengo un coche’. Wɔ English mu, ɛnyɛ ɛkɛ ne ‘have’ (I have a car) na ɛnyɛ ‘have got’ (I have got a car). ‘Have got’ wɔ British English mu paa na wɔhyɛ no wɔ nkyɛn kyɛn mu. Nneɛma no wɔ hɔ gyina, nanso ‘have got’ wɔ hɔ wɔ present tense mu. Wɔ negative na question mu, ‘have got’ no hyɛ ‘have’ ahyɛ bosom, ɛnyɛ ‘do/does’. Ɛyɛ: ‘I haven’t got a car’ na ‘Have you got a car?’.
rule: ‘Have got / Has got’ no wɔ hɔ ma yɛka biribi a ɔte ase yɛn ho, abofra, sɛnea yɛte, na nneɛma a yɛho yɛn ho adwuma. Affirmative: I/you/we/they have got, he/she/it has got. Negative: I/you/we/they have not got (haven't got), he/she/it has not got (hasn't got). Questions: Have I/you/we/they got? Has he/she/it got? ‘Do/does’ ɛto so. Wɔ short questions mu: Yes, I have / No, I haven't. Wɔhyɛ no wɔ present tense mu; wɔ other tenses mu, wɔhyɛ ‘have’ ho.

concept_examples.text: I have got a new phone.

concept_examples.translation: ɔbaa no ani so taa so.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu, ‘tener’ ka ‘have’ anaa ‘have got’. Nanso ‘have got’ no hyɛ ‘got’ ahyɛ bosom, ɛnyɛ ‘get’. Sɛ woaka ‘I have get’ a, ɛyɛ error, efisɛ wɔka ‘get’ a wɔ infinitive mu. Bu: ‘have got’ no wɔ hɔ ma yɛka biribi a ɔte ase yɛn ho wɔ present tense mu.

examples.original: We have got a big house.
examples.translation: Yɛn wɔ yɛn house bi a ɛte sɛeɛ.
examples.note: Yɛhyɛ ‘have got’ ma yɛka biribi a ɔte ase yɛn ho.
Yɛhyɛ ‘has got’ ma yɛka biribi a ɔte ase ɔno ho.
Negative no yɛ ‘hasn't got’.
Question no yɛ ‘have/has’ na subject no a wɔayɛ.

title: Nsεmfa a wɔnkyerε no (in, on, under, next to)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka 'wɔ' ho nhiaa: 'wɔ ba', 'wɔ tɛtia', 'wɔ mu'. Wɔ Asa, wɔyɛ nsεmfa a wɔnkyerε no pii, na ɛsɛe nea ɛbɛka no so. 'In' de ama wɔn a wɔyɛ anidaso anaa wɔyɛ 3D (in the room), 'on' de ama wɔn a wɔyɛ ase (on the table), 'under' de ama wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ (under the bed) na 'next to' de ama wɔn a wɔwɔ po (next to the door). Sɛe nso sɛ 'wɔ kona' ka de 'on the corner' (nni 'in').
rule: Nsεmfa a wɔnkyerε no a ɛyɛ ɔha: in (wɔ mu), on (wɔ so), under (wɔ hɔ), next to (wɔ po). Nso: behind (wɔ mu), in front of (wɔ anim), between (wɔ mmienu). Wɔ Asa Britian, sɛ ɛbɛka yɛn ho a, wɔka 'on the bus', 'on the train', nanso 'in the car'. Wɔmfa ho: 'Where is the cat?' → 'It is under the table.'

concept_examples.text: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the bed.
The supermarket is next to the bank.
concept_examples.translation: Supi ma no wɔ banco no po.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈsuːpəmɑːkɪt ɪz nekst tə ðə bæŋk/

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛka 'wɔ trotro no' ho nhiaa, nanso wɔ Asa, sɛ ɛbɛka yɛn ho a (trotro, train, plane), wɔnka 'on', nni 'in'. 'In' de ama car na taxi (in the car).

examples.original: The milk is in the fridge.
examples.translation: Mma no wɔ fridge no mu.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'in' ama wɔn a wɔyɛ anidaso.

examples.original: The keys are on the table.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'on' ama wɔn a wɔyɛ ase.

examples.original: My shoes are under the chair.
examples.translation: Me ntoma wɔ chair no hɔ.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'under' ama wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ.

examples.original: The school is next to the church.
examples.phonetic: /ðə skuːl ɪz nekst tə ðə tʃɜːtʃ/
examples.translation: School no wɔ church no po.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'next to' ama wɔn a wɔwɔ po.

title: Demostrativos (this, that, these, those)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛn nni 'ɛyi' (nkyɛn), 'ɛno' (ntɛm), na 'ɛnna' (kɛse). Wɔ English, wɔn nni nnɛm baako: 'this' (singular) na 'these' (plural) ma ɛyɛ nkyɛn; 'that' (singular) na 'those' (plural) ma ɛyɛ kɛse. Nkɔsoɔ a ɛso Twi abuafo no, yɛnntɔn 'ɛno' ne 'ɛnna' kyerɛw wɔ English, na yɛde 'this' kyerɛkyerɛ biribiara a yɛhu, ɛmfa ho a ɛkɛse. Enti, wɔde 'these' (ɛnni) ama 'this' (ɛyi) a wɔde asɛm bu wɔn no ho.
rule: Yɛde 'this' ma obi anaa nnuan a ɛwɔ yɛn nkyɛn (singular). Yɛde 'these' ma nnuan a ɛwɔ yɛn nkyɛn (plural). Yɛde 'that' ma obi anaa nnuan a ɛkɛse (singular). Yɛde 'those' ma nnuan a ɛkɛse (plural). Yɛde wɔn ma wɔ akwan mu: 'This is my friend' (sɛ ɔwɔ hɔ) na 'That is my house' (sɛ yɛrekyerɛ ɛkɛse).

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, 'ɛyi' ne 'ɛnni' wɔ hɔ gyina, nanso Twi abuafo bi de 'this' ma plural anaa wɔde 'these' /ðiːz/ ne 'this' /ðɪs/ asɛm bu wɔn ho. Fa so sɛ, 'this' yɛ singular na 'these' yɛ plural.

examples.note: Nnua a ɛwɔ nkyɛn no singular.
Nnuan a ɛwɔ nkyɛn no plural.
Nnua a ɛkɛse no singular.
Nnuan a ɛkɛse no plural.

title: Can (ability and permission)
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnkyɛm 'sɛ' ka ho asɛm ne adwuma a ɔwɔ kwan so (me sɛ me tumi ayɛ adwuma, ɔsɛ ɔbɛka me). Wɔ English mu, 'can' ma yɛn nkyɛn asɛm no mu mmienu no nyinaa. Nnipa pii a wɔtumi bu no a ɛno ara nso ɛnyɛ sɛ ɔbɛka 'to' a ɛbɛba n’agyina (I can swim, ɛnyɛ sɛ I can to swim). Enti sɛ wopɛ sɛ wubu asɛm bi ka kyerɛɛ wo mmara anaa wo tumi, wo mmara, na ɛno akyi wo ne wo de wo kwan ma no (Can you swim?) anaa wo de 'not' ma no (I cannot / can't). Ɛyɛ modal verb enti ɛno akyi ɛsɛ sɛ wobɛka verb a ɛnni 'to' akyi.
rule: 'Can' de ma: 1) tumi (I can play the piano), 2) mmara (Can I go to the bathroom?), 3) akwan (It can rain tomorrow). Ɛnyɛ sɛ ɔbɛka akyire abiɛsa biara. Kyerɛkyerɛ: I/you/he/she/it/we/they can + verb base. Kyerɛkyerɛ: cannot (can't) + verb base. Asɛm a wobu: Can + subject + verb base? Kyerɛkyerɛ: Yes, I can / No, I can't.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu yɛka 'me sɛ me tumi asɛm' anaa 'ɔsɛ ɔbɛka me' anaa ɛno ara. Wɔ English mu, 'can' akyi ɛsɛ sɛ wobɛka verb a ɛnni 'to' akyi. Sɛ woka 'can to' a, ɛyɛ kwan a ɛyɛ den paa efisɛ ɛde yɛn asɛm a ɛwɔ hɔ a wɔde 'to' ma no (want to, need to).

examples.note: Tumi a ɛyɛ den.

examples.translation: Wode ma me de me phone?
examples.note: Kyerɛ sɛ wopɛ mmara.
Kwan a ɛnyɛ ne 'can't'.

levels.label: Questions and short answers
levels.translation: Asɛm a wobu ne kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ firi

examples.original: Can they come? Yes, they can.
examples.note: Asɛm a wobu ne kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ firi.

title: Wh- (what, where, who, when) asɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbisa asɛm a wɔde 'dɛn', 'he', 'na ɔyɛ', 'bere'. Wɔ Gyeman nee wɔn a wɔde 'what' (dɛn), 'where' (he), 'who' (na ɔyɛ), 'when' (bere). Sɛnea wɔde bɛka ne: Wh- asɛm + kɔkɔbɔ verb (anaa 'to be' verb) + ɔkyerɛwɔ + kyerɛwɔ verb? Sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ne: 'Where do you live?' (He wɔde a wɔnfa wo?). Ɛyɛ anigye sɛ woahu wo ho ase ma woatwa 'do/does' wɔ present simple, na wommusua ɔkwan no wɔ indirect questions (sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ne 'Can you tell me where the station is?' – ɛyɛ, na 'where is the station' mmom ɛnyɛ indirect).
rule: Wh- asɛm a wɔde bɛka ne: 1) Sɛ ɛyɛ 'to be' verb: Wh- asɛm + am/is/are + ɔkyerɛwɔ? (Where is the bank?). 2) Sɛ ɛyɛ 'can': Wh- asɛm + can + ɔkyerɛwɔ + verb? (What can you do?). 3) Sɛ ɛyɛ present simple (verbs foforo): Wh- asɛm + do/does + ɔkyerɛwɔ + base verb? (What do you eat?). 4) Wɔ indirect questions (a wɔde 'Can you tell me...', 'Do you know...'), ɔkwan no ne ɔkyerɛwɔ + verb (no inversion): 'Can you tell me where the station is?' (na 'where is the station' mmom ɛnyɛ indirect).

common_error.wrong: Can you tell me where is the station?
common_error.correct: Can you tell me where the station is?
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, wɔ indirect questions, yɛntwa ɔkwan a yɛde wɔ direct questions: 'Womfa me he a ɛwɔ station no?' Wɔ Gyeman, wɔ indirect questions, ɔkwan no ne ɔkyerɛwɔ + verb, no inversion. Ɛyɛ anigye sɛ wɔde ɛno ara wɔ Gyeman.

examples.note: Asɛm a wɔde ma wahu dɛn.
Asɛm a wɔde ma wahu he.

examples.translation: Na ɔyɛ ɔkyerɛwɔ a ɔwɔ wo?
examples.note: Asɛm a wɔde ma wahu na ɔyɛ.
Asɛm a wɔde ma wahu bere.

title: There is / Wɔ wɔ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka 'wɔ wɔ' yɛnka sɛ: 'wɔ wɔ'. Wɔ Gyeman nee Ahere, wɔhyɛ dwumawɔfoɔ: 'there is' (kɔmfa) nee 'there are' (mmoa). Adwuma a yɛbɛka no kɔ so ara na yɛde no. Ɛtɔ, 'There is a book on the table' (Wɔ wɔ akɔntɔ a wɔ tɔro no so), 'There are two books on the table' (Wɔ wɔ akɔntɔ mmienu wɔ tɔro no so). Yɛde no wɔmfa hu: 'Is there a bank near here?' nee 'Are there any restaurants?'. Adwuma a ɛda Hispanicfoɔ so ara na wɔde 'there is/are' nee 'have' yiyi (wɔka sɛ 'The house has a garden' na ɛnneɛ 'There is a garden in the house').
rule: Yɛde 'There is' ma kɔmfa nee nnwuma a ɛnyɛ mmoa (There is some water). Yɛde 'There are' ma mmoa (There are three chairs). Wɔmfa: Is there...? / Are there...? Wɔ mfatoho: There isn't / There aren't. Yɛde no nee 'any' wɔmfa nee mfatoho: 'Is there any milk?' (Wɔ wɔ nsa?) nee 'There isn't any milk' (Nsa nni).

common_error.wrong: In my house have a garden.
common_error.correct: There is a garden in my house.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛka sɛ 'Me baabi wɔ garden' yɛde 'tener', nanso wɔ Gyeman, sɛ yɛbɛka ɛwɔ hɔ, yɛde 'there is/are', ɛnni 'have'. Ɛyɛ kwan a wɔde asɛm biara ka no. Yɛmmɔ sɛ 'My house has a garden' (tener) sɛ ɛyɛ ɔlɛ, nanso 'there is' yɛ nokware wɔ hɔ a wɔ wɔ.
